subject: Signal mapping & billing ownership for per-route latency/cost signals
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, ira.gomez@acme-data.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Signal mapping & billing ownership for per-route latency/cost signals

Hi team —

Following yesterday's sync with Acme (Ira copied), they want a single-pane view that ties per-route latency signals to per-route cost attribution so their platform team can spot regressions that impact unit economics.

Asking for a practical, prioritized plan we can commit to for the next sprint:

- Minimal deliverable (MVP): a per-route dashboard tile that shows 7d latency p50/p95, token cost per 1k tokens, and request count.
- Ownership question: who owns the billing attribution column — Product (Marissa) or Observability/Telemetry (Karthik/Evelyn)? This affects where the source-of-truth lives.
- Exception flow: when a route's cost delta exceeds 20% and latency p95 rises 25% we want an automated runbook link and an on-call paging policy.

I've attached a rough signal catalog and a quick mockup. Can each of you comment on feasibility and a proposed owner for the billing rows?

Thanks —
Naomi
Head of Customer Success (Platform)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: per-route-signal-catalog.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: proposed-dashboard-sketch.png (png)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, ira.gomez@acme-data.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Signal mapping & billing ownership for per-route latency/cost signals

Naomi —

Thanks for the concise ask and the attachments, very helpful. High level thoughts:

- MVP is sensible. Product can own the dashboard UX and gating criteria for alerts. We should define the canonical billing numbers (per-route token cost) though — I'd prefer Observability to be the producer of that metric (so it's emitted in telemetry), and Product to be the consumer.
- Feasibility: Karthik, can we get per-route tokenized cost emitted as a metric? If not, we need a short pipeline job that joins usage counts + model cost per-token to produce a time-series.
- Exception flow: Product will author the initial runbook content and escalation policy. Ops should wire the automation.

Proposed owners:
- Billing attribution metric: Observability (Karthik)
- Dashboard UX and alert thresholds: Product (Marissa)
- Runbook & automation: Shared; Product writes, Ops implements.

Ira — if this aligns with Acme's expectations let us know what cadence you'd like for the first demo (we can schedule next week).

— Marissa
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, ira.gomez@acme-data.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Signal mapping & billing ownership for per-route latency/cost signals

Marissa/Naomi —

We can produce a per-route cost time-series but a couple caveats:

1) Source data: We only have token counts per request in analytics. Mapping token counts to cost requires attaching a model-cost-per-token rate (varies by model variant). We can support two approaches:
   - Emit a computed metric in the serving path (adds ~3ms p95 overhead in our microbenchmarks) — good for real-time dashboards.
   - Offline pipeline job that aggregates hourly and writes the time-series to the metrics store (no serving overhead, but coarser granularity).
2) Cardinality: customers with many routes (1000s) will increase storage and query cost. We should sample or cap the default to top-200 routes by request volume, with on-demand expansion.
3) Exception detection: fine to wire an automated alert. Need Product to confirm the exact thresholds and whether this should trigger a page or just an async ticket.

Given the Acme ask and the timeline, recommend MVP timeline:
- This sprint: instrument computed metric for top-200 routes (pipeline approach).
- Next sprint: product dashboard tile + alert wiring.

I'll open an Obs ticket and a small spike to estimate engineering effort (OBS-1129).

— Karthik
Engineering, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ira.gomez@acme-data.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Signal mapping & billing ownership for per-route latency/cost signals

Looping back with operational constraints and next steps:

- Agree with proposed owners: Observability produces the billing metric, Product owns thresholds and runbook content, Ops (SRE) implements the escalation workflow.
- Paging: for initial launch we'll send pages to the Observability on-call when the exception rule fires (20% cost delta + 25% p95 increase). Product will get a Slack channel notification and a JIRA automation to create a post-incident review ticket.
- Storage/cost: we'll default to top-200 routes and keep 90-day retention for the per-route cost series; advise Acme about cost implications.

Next steps / owners:
- Karthik: open OBS-1129 and attach the per-route-signal-catalog.xlsx, estimate spike (due EOD Wed).
- Marissa: prepare the dashboard acceptance criteria and initial runbook draft (due next Tue).
- Naomi: coordinate demo with Acme and confirm their top-20 routes to prioritize.

Evelyn
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
